title: Walk/Zeta correspondence for quantum walks on path graphs: a pre-geometric structure implied by a generalized reflection principle
authors: Jiro Akahori, Riki Kitano, Norio Konno, Iwao Sato
abstract: We establish a local Konno-Sato correspondence for reflected random and Szegedy walks on a finite path graph. A generalized reflection principle, using explicit involutions rather than point reflections in the asymmetric case, yields exact zeta factorizations into a boundary factor and local factors indexed by the infinite dihedral group. After symmetrization, the classical and quantum local factors correspond for each group element. The identity contribution determines the normalized thermodynamic limits. In the symmetric case, diffusive and ballistic scalings recover the Gaussian Poisson summation formula and the Dirac comb identity, respectively. Under a double scaling of the asymmetry and spectral parameter, the quantum factorization yields a massive Dirac-type limit: nonidentity even words produce the periodic-orbit factor, the identity produces the free-field factor, and odd words together with the boundary produce a finite boundary correction.
summary: This work establishes a deep mathematical correspondence between the zeta functions describing quantum walks on finite paths and continuum spectral determinants. By analyzing the factorization of the discrete zeta function in various limits, the authors show that the discrete structure acts as a 'pre-geometric skeleton' whose continuum limit is governed by the massive Dirac operator. This links quantum walk dynamics to fundamental results in spectral geometry.
main_problem: The paper investigates the 'Walk/Zeta correspondence' by establishing a relationship between the zeta functions of quantum walks on finite path graphs and continuum trace formulas.
main_result: The discrete zeta function factorizes into components indexed by the infinite dihedral group, and in the continuum limit, this product matches the Gelfand–Yaglom determinant of a massive Dirac operator.
method: The authors use a generalized reflection principle and a local Konno–Sato correspondence to derive exact discrete trace formulas, which are then analyzed in various scaling limits.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum walk (Szegedy walk) and a classical random walk on a finite path graph ($P_N$) with reflecting boundaries and arbitrary spatial asymmetry. The analysis compares these discrete systems to their infinite-line counterparts.
key_observables: Zeta functions ($\det(I - uP(N))^{-1}$), the boundary factor, and the local factors indexed by the dihedral group.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of the generalized reflection principle and the local Konno–Sato correspondence to establish the factorization.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the discrete factorization of the zeta function, then analyzing the convergence of this factorization in the thermodynamic, diffusive, and ballistic limits, culminating in the identification of the continuum limit with the massive Dirac operator determinant.
why_interesting: The connection between discrete spectral identities (quantum walks) and continuous spectral theory (Dirac operators) via zeta regularization is a powerful tool for understanding spectral properties in quantum systems, linking lattice physics to continuum field theory.
